entities.name: Abbo of Auxerre
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Abbo of Auxerre (died c. 860) was a Benedictine bishop of Auxerre in Burgundy, serving one of the most intellectually distinguished sees in the Carolingian Church. Auxerre had produced a remarkable sequence of scholarly bishops in the Carolingian period, and Abbo contributed to the cathedral school and administrative life of the diocese during the reign of Charles the Bald.

Auxerre's cathedral school was a significant centre of Carolingian learning, and the see's bishops included figures of European intellectual importance. Auxerre's scholarly tradition drew on its connections with the Carolingian court schools and with the Abbey of Saint-Germain d'Auxerre, one of Burgundy's most important monastic centres. Abbo's episcopate participated in the continuing project of Carolingian ecclesiastical reform that sought to elevate clerical education and liturgical standards across the Frankish Church.

His abbacy at Auxerre coincided with the political turbulence of Charles the Bald's reign, when the western Frankish kingdom was contested both internally and by Viking raiders. Bishops like Abbo occupied the difficult position of royal administrators and Church governors in a period when the distinction between ecclesiastical and secular authority was still being negotiated across the Carolingian territories.
